content.title: About
content.content: Ladoo is a traditional Indian sweet ball made from roasted gram flour, sugar, clarified butter (ghee), and aromatic spices. It has a soft, slightly sticky texture and a rich fragrance typical of South Asian desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ladoo are commonly served at festivals, weddings, and religious ceremonies across India and South Asia.
There are many variations: besan (chickpea) ladoo, coconut ladoo, sunflower seed ladoo, and even gluten‑free versions.
Traditionally, the mixture is hand‑rolled into small spheres about 2–3 cm in diameter.
The word “ladoo” comes from the Sanskrit “लडु”, meaning “ball” or “round”.
In some regions, ladoo are decorated with edible gold leaf or nut crumbs.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and ghee provide a quick supply of calories, making ladoo a good energy boost after physical activity.

items.title: Rich in micronutrients
items.content: The gram flour used in many recipes contains magnesium, iron, and zinc, essential for metabolic functions.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Spices such as cardamom and cloves have antioxidant effects that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Ladoo contain a significant amount of sugar, so people with diabetes or those watching their weight should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Nut allergy risk
items.content: Gram flour or added nuts can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of ghee and sugar, a 30 g serving of ladoo can contain roughly 150 kcal.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ladoo are enjoyed as a dessert or snack, often paired with tea. They can be kept in a dry container and eaten one or several at a time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ladoo in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to prevent the ghee from melting.
